# Jubilees Chapter 33 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Reuben's sin; Rachel dies; Leah dies

---

**33:1** Jacob moved south and camped at the tower of the flock, between Ephrath and Bethlehem.

**33:2** It was there that Rachel died. Jacob buried her at Ephrath — which is Bethlehem — and put up a stone marker over her grave beside the road. It's still there today.

**33:3** During this period, Reuben slept with Bilhah, his father's concubine. When Jacob found out, he was both furious and heartbroken.

**33:4** He confronted Reuben, and Reuben admitted everything and asked forgiveness. Jacob forgave him. But from that day on, Jacob never slept with Bilhah again.

**33:5** In his mind, what happened was an enormous violation — his son had defiled his own father's bed. He kept his distance from Bilhah entirely.

**33:6** This is why Israel was commanded: never sleep with your father's wife. To do so is to violate your father.

**33:7** Any man who sleeps with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness — and the penalty for that is death.

**33:8** And if a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, the law is the same: both are to be put to death by fire.

**33:9** Every form of sexual immorality and unlawful union is catalogued in the heavenly tablets — written and permanent.

**33:10** After Rachel died, Jacob brought Leah with him when he went to visit his father Isaac. Isaac was overjoyed to see Jacob, Leah, and all the grandchildren.

**33:11** This visit to Isaac at Mamre — in Hebron — was in the forty-fifth jubilee, third week, fourth year.

**33:12** Isaac was ancient by now; his eyes had failed completely and he was blind.

**33:13** "Don't be sad, Father," Jacob said. "I'm back. I've done well — I have large flocks and herds, and your grandchildren are all grown."

**33:14** Isaac prayed over Jacob and gave him a joyful blessing. Jacob remained close to his father for the rest of Isaac's life.

**33:15** In the forty-fifth jubilee, fourth week, first year, Leah died. Jacob buried her at night in the cave at Machpelah near Mamre, alongside Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, and Rebekah.

**33:16** The grief was profound — Jacob mourned deeply, and all of Leah's sons cried for her.

**33:17** God comforted Jacob in his grief.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The Reuben episode in Jubilees is more merciful than Genesis 49:4 — Jacob forgives but separates. The transformation of Reuben's sin into a founding legal case (vv.6-9) illustrates Jubilees' consistent narrative-to-law technique. The night burial of Leah (v.15) at Machpelah is a detail unique to Jubilees.*
